text.p: Northland Cranberries Inc said it is "on track" in its efforts to increase its long-term crop purchase agreements with other independent growers.
"We have 27 growers under contract, representing approximately 1,500 acres of fruit in various stages of maturity," said president John Swendrowski in a statement.

"Our corporate goal is to double our fruit supply within the next five years. Through our expanding grower contract program and our aggressive acquisition strategy, we are on track toward achieving that goal," he added.
Northland has 2,548 planted acres of cranberries and more than 23,000 acres of support land.
Earlier, the company reported February 28 second-quarter earnings of $0.11 per share on revenues of $13.5 million. A year ago, it earned $0.01 per share on revenues of $4 million.
As a result of the company's changed business strategy, comparisons of the financial results between the fiscal 1997 and 1996 periods are not meaningful.

Northland said its performance during the latest second quarter reflects a continuation of its "marsh to market" business strategy. This strategy involves retaining possession of the company's annual cranberry crop and producing and selling value-added cranberry products throughout the year.
In previous years, the majority of the annual fall crop was presold during long-term fixed price contracts to cranberry product processors.
